matches.quote: Normalising by F_z, the varied quantity, hides the true F_z dependence at fixed F_ac and diverges as F_z → 0.
Figs. 2b, 2d and 3 show β1 crossing zero in a structure with a hard-wall surface barrier, abrupt interfaces, homogeneous strain, uniform F_z and no alloy disorder.
The model assumes a fully strained, defect-free 15 nm Ge layer (up to 25 nm in Fig. 2a–b) coherent on relaxed Ge0.84Sn0.16, a mismatch of roughly 2–2.5% in tension.
The abstract and conclusion state that the large in-plane g-factor (g∥^c ≈ −8, Fig. 2e) "facilitates the integration of superconductors", but no calculation addresses this.
The large F_z dependence of g⊥ (Figs. 2a, 2c, 3) and of β1 implies a large ∂ω/∂F_z and hence sensitivity to electric-field noise.
The 6-band k·p model omits the conduction band, which may matter most in this strongly tensile regime.
The perturbative effective models may fail close to the features of interest, and no non-perturbative check is shown.
The surface barrier is idealised and unspecified, yet it creates the asymmetry that sets F_z*.
replace the hard wall with a finite barrier ... and discuss the interface trap and fixed-charge densities typical of Ge MOS interfaces
Give the actual confinement energies ħω_x, ħω_y ... so readers can judge whether l_x = 35 nm and l_y = 60 nm are realistic for gate-defined dots.
Panel (b) uses x = 10% while (c) and the rest of the paper use x = 16%; use x = 16% throughout or explain the difference.
A k·p envelope model with a hard wall cannot capture interface-inversion-asymmetry terms ... Inhomogeneous strain from the gate electrodes ... would add further residual SOI at F_z*.
With top gates alone, F_z is not an independent knob at fixed dot occupancy.
The authors should give Ω in MHz for a stated drive ... and compare in the same framework with a planar Ge/SiGe HH dot ... and with Ge/Si nanowire
Without this, the claimed qubit advantages and the comparison with the "spinless" qubit proposal (Ref. 63) are not supported.
The advance over the authors' earlier work should be stated explicitly. Refs. 56 and 57 already established the large linear Rashba term of LH Ge/GeSn wells.

notes: C13 asks specifically whether alloy disorder in GeSn could prevent the LH character of the ground state; P5, P18 and P25 discuss alloy disorder, Sn compositional fluctuations/segregation and strain relaxation affecting the LH ground state and F_z*, so C13 is judged 'partly'. C15 asks both for the justification of B0 = 0.05 T and the Fig. 3 normalization; P1 and P14 critique the Fig. 3 normalization without asking why 0.05 T was chosen ('partly'). C4 could not be checked by the review because the Supplemental Material was not provided with the manuscript.
